claim: Five model families reach test AUROC 0.8229-0.8429 for LUXSMED>=8.2 kPa from 10 routine predictors
limitation: Modest PR-AUC (~0.35-0.37) at 9.31% prevalence
recommended_wording: Five model families achieved statistically indistinguishable discrimination (test AUROC 0.823-0.843)
do_not_claim: Do not claim strong/excellent discrimination or clinical-grade accuracy

claim: 0/10 pairwise model comparisons significant after BH-FDR; no model family is superior
limitation: Pooled 182-test FDR shows XGB vs MLP p=0.0136 (secondary)
recommended_wording: No pairwise model comparison was significant after multiple-testing correction
do_not_claim: Do not claim XGBoost (or any model) is the best/superior model

claim: Class-balanced models over-predict raw risk (OOF intercepts -2.24 to -1.86); OOF Platt scaling corrects aggregate calibration on the locked test without changing AUROC
limitation: Mechanism is prior-shift (primary explanation); isotonic rejected (466 OOF positives)
recommended_wording: Class-balancing produced severe raw over-prediction that out-of-fold Platt scaling corrected without altering discrimination
do_not_claim: Do not claim subgroup or universal calibration adequacy

claim: Normal-BMI sensitivity is 27.1-47.7 pp lower than Obese in all 5 models (FDR q<=0.006)
limitation: Normal-BMI has 22 test positives (wide CIs); model-fairness fact distinct from cohort missingness fact; non-causal
recommended_wording: Sensitivity was 27-48 percentage points lower in normal-weight than obese participants across all five models
do_not_claim: Do not claim the mechanism is causal or that BMI fairness was mitigated

claim: The BMI-Obese vs Normal sensitivity disparity is stable across 8.0 kPa; CAND_2; CAND_3 (15/15) and enlarged temporally to 62.8-71.9 pp
limitation: Temporal result is PARTIAL replication; 8.0 kPa is relabel-only
recommended_wording: The obese-BMI sensitivity disparity reproduced across all sensitivity analyses and a later NHANES cycle where it enlarged
do_not_claim: Do not present the temporal reproduction as full or external validation

claim: Age-60+ sensitivity is lower than Age-40-59 in 5/5 models; FDR-significant in 4/5 (not Logistic)
limitation: Significance lost in 9/12 sensitivity-cohort instances; direction reverses temporally; non-monotonic (peak ~65y)
recommended_wording: Older participants showed a consistent-direction sensitivity deficit that was significant in four of five models and specification-sensitive; SECONDARY OBSERVATION per MANUSCRIPT_FRAMING_GUIDANCE.md -- Results body + Limitations only, not the abstract, not a co-headline with the BMI finding
do_not_claim: Do not claim Age-60+ significance in 5/5 or a monotone older-is-worse gradient; do not present the Age-60+ sensitivity disparity in the abstract or as a co-primary subgroup finding

claim: Split conformal (alpha=0.10) meets marginal coverage overall (88.12-90.82%)
limitation: Marginal validity is a guarantee under exchangeability only
recommended_wording: Split-conformal prediction met its 90% marginal coverage target overall
do_not_claim: Do not extend marginal validity to any subgroup

claim: Subgroup conformal coverage fails for BMI-Obese (76.8-82.3%) and Age-60+ (81.1-85.6%) in all 5 models (CIs exclude 90%); Normal-BMI/Overweight over-cover
limitation: Empirical; one cohort (CAND_1); small subgroup precision; documentation/MASTER_RESEARCH_RESULTS.md misreports this (conflict C1)
recommended_wording: Marginal coverage concealed under-coverage of obese and older participants in every model
do_not_claim: Do not claim conditional/subgroup conformal validity; do not cite MASTER_RESEARCH_RESULTS.md conformal numbers

claim: BMI-Obese intersect Age-60+ baseline conformal coverage collapses to 64.97-75.17% (test N=294; 35 positive)
limitation: Descriptive; pre-specified small cell (N=294); the overlap is 13.7% of test not 62% (that is the union)
recommended_wording: In the obese-and-60+ intersection (N=294) baseline conformal coverage fell to 65-75%
do_not_claim: Do not describe the intersection as ~62% of the cohort or claim a causal interaction

claim: FDR-gated Mondrian conformal recalibration restored nominal coverage in 5/9 targeted model-subgroup combinations
limitation: 4/9 targets unresolved; XGBoost marginal coverage 93.4% breaches +/-5 pp tolerance (+5.27 pp); overlap uses Age-over-BMI last-write-wins precedence not joint mitigation
recommended_wording: Group-wise conformal recalibration partially not fully repaired subgroup coverage
do_not_claim: Do not claim Phase 7 resolved subgroup coverage or the BMI classification disparity

claim: No acceptable BMI-sensitivity mitigation was identified across four candidate strategies on an independent split
limitation: Only MLP got a candidate (BMI-Platt: gap 39.03->34.48 pp); no formal candidate inference
recommended_wording: A dedicated re-analysis of four BMI-targeted mitigation strategies identified none meeting the pre-specified multi-metric acceptance criteria
do_not_claim: Do not claim a universal or cross-family BMI mitigation

claim: Subgroup-specific probability calibration did not improve subgroup reliability or fairness beyond global Platt scaling; classification decisions unchanged
limitation: No joint calibrator; no candidate inference; runtime access order only partially proven; one duplicate output lacks provenance
recommended_wording: Subgroup calibration did not improve subgroup reliability or fairness and left classifications unchanged
do_not_claim: Do not claim subgroup calibration solved BMI fairness or provided joint intersectional calibration

claim: No acceptable XGBoost retuning within the authorized candidate family removes its post-mitigation conformal coverage-tolerance breach
limitation: Every gap-closing candidate costs 11-22 pp overall sensitivity or flips the breach
recommended_wording: Retuning XGBoost within the authorized family did not remove its post-mitigation coverage breach
do_not_claim: Do not claim the XGBoost breach is resolvable

claim: Joint intersectional conformal calibration (Method b/c; M4b N0=0) restores Obese-and-60+ coverage on CAND_1 for most models but breaches marginal tolerance for XGB/LGBM and does not replicate temporally (1/5)
audit_status: VERIFIED (C2 ADJUDICATED 2026-08-27: executed 2026-08-24, EXPLORATORY only; stale status-CSV row superseded)
lineage_status: ESTABLISHED (joint artifact generating lineage NOT FOUND)
limitation: Joint calibration cell N=138; generating script/manifest/runtime log NOT FOUND IN REPOSITORY
recommended_wording: An exploratory joint-cell conformal calibration restored intersectional coverage on the primary cohort for most models but breached the marginal tolerance for two and did not replicate on a later cycle
do_not_claim: Do not present joint mitigation as primary or as a solution to intersectional coverage

claim: Withholding Non-Hispanic Black participants from training reduces discrimination on that subgroup (AUROC 0.7719-0.7893) and destabilizes calibration
dataset: CAND_1 non-NHB train N=5366 / NHB holdout N=1787
limitation: Within-NHANES demographic holdout; NHB holdout positive count varies by source column
recommended_wording: A within-NHANES demographic holdout showed moderate discrimination loss and unstable calibration on the withheld subgroup
do_not_claim: Do not call the NHB holdout external validation

claim: Discrimination; calibration correction; and the BMI-Obese disparity are robust to an 8.0-kPa cutoff; the full re-run concludes SOME MAJOR FINDINGS ARE THRESHOLD-SENSITIVE
lineage_status: ESTABLISHED (frozen 8.2 protocol commit + model manifest NOT FOUND)
limitation: 8.2 kPa is PRIMARY; 8.0 kPa is a sensitivity analysis; Age-60+ significance is threshold-sensitive
recommended_wording: A robustness analysis at 8.0 kPa left discrimination and the obese-BMI disparity intact but confirmed the older-age disparity's significance is threshold-sensitive
do_not_claim: Do not replace the primary 8.2 kPa analysis with 8.0 kPa; do not claim 8.0 and 8.2 are statistically indistinguishable

claim: CAND_2 (N=7639) AUROC 0.8526-0.8572 and CAND_3 (N=3582; 12 predictors) AUROC 0.8280-0.8457 reproduce the primary qualitative pattern
limitation: Age-60+ significance lost in CAND_2 (3/4) and CAND_3 (4/4)
recommended_wording: Two independently constructed cohorts reproduced the primary discrimination and obese-BMI fairness findings
do_not_claim: Do not claim the age finding is robust across cohorts

claim: Targeted multiple imputation for the Non-Hispanic Black selection question changed AUROC by <0.007 and NHB sensitivity by <=+/-4.2 pp (all CIs include 0; BH adj p=0.978)
dataset: MI pool N=7768 vs complete-case N=7153
limitation: Narrow scope (NHB question only); BH q=0.978 is a correction-ceiling artifact; 4/5 STABLE MLP INDETERMINATE
recommended_wording: A targeted multiple-imputation analysis did not materially change discrimination or the Non-Hispanic Black sensitivity estimate
do_not_claim: Do not claim MI and complete-case are equivalent or extend MI to whole-cohort conclusions

claim: MI conformal reliability is descriptively consistent with complete-case; BMI-Obese under-coverage persists under MI
limitation: No executable MI-conformal source/models/scores/runtime log/equivalence test/Rubin pooling
recommended_wording: An exploratory multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis produced conformal subgroup coverage consistent with the complete-case results
do_not_claim: Do not cite MI conformal as load-bearing evidence or claim pooled inference/equivalence

claim: ALT; AST; BMI; and Age are the top four predictors across all five model families
limitation: Association with model output not causal
recommended_wording: Model predictions were driven by established markers of hepatic injury and metabolic risk (ALT AST BMI age)
do_not_claim: Do not make causal claims from feature importance

claim: All five models show positive net benefit vs treat-all/treat-none across p_t ~0.05-0.35 including within BMI-Obese and Age-60+
limitation: Internal cohort only; net-benefit curves not a deployment endpoint
recommended_wording: Decision-curve analysis showed net benefit over default strategies within the plausible threshold range
do_not_claim: Do not claim demonstrated clinical utility or deployment readiness

claim: NHANES 2021-2023 (N=4910; 11.47%) yields AUROC 0.7765-0.7824; persistent/enlarged BMI-Obese disparity (62.8-71.9 pp); persistent subgroup conformal under-coverage; and M4b intersectional success for 1/5 models; final status PARTIAL TEMPORAL REPLICATION
limitation: Later-cycle frozen-model evaluation; not clinical readiness/causal/external; root cause = SUPPORTED ASSOCIATION only
recommended_wording: A later NHANES cycle partially replicated the findings: discrimination declined; the obese-BMI disparity persisted and enlarged; and frozen intersectional conformal protection largely failed
do_not_claim: Do not call this full temporal replication or external validation

claim: No compatible independent non-NHANES cohort was obtained; external validation was not performed
limitation: No dataset with VCTE LUXSMED>=8.2 kPa and the 10 routine labs identified
recommended_wording: External validation on an independent non-NHANES population has not been performed and is the study's foremost limitation
do_not_claim: Do not claim any external validation

claim: CAND_4 all-ages (>=12 y) cohort N=8215 was constructed but never modeled
limitation: Documentation tension over its frozen tracking status (conflict C4); no result artifact
recommended_wording: An all-ages cohort was defined but not analysed; the study is adult-scoped
do_not_claim: Do not report any CAND_4 performance

claim: Pre-registered severity-graded secondary outcomes executed as a relabel-only descriptive pass (Amendment #15): >=9.7 kPa AUROC 0.85-0.86, >=13.6 kPa 0.84-0.86 (comparable to primary); frozen 8.2-kPa Platt recalibration does not transport to the rarer outcomes
limitation: Relabel-only: no per-outcome retraining or Platt refit; >=13.6 kPa overall-only (59 test positives); >=9.7 kPa BMI fairness underpowered (Normal-BMI n=11 test positives); no FDR
recommended_wording: Severity-graded secondary outcomes (advanced fibrosis >=9.7 kPa, cirrhosis >=13.6 kPa) showed discrimination comparable to the primary outcome, but the primary-outcome recalibration did not transport to the lower-prevalence definitions
